# INDRA-Sat-Diff - results summary (auto-generated by make_results_figs.py)

Source: `artifacts/results/sac_2025/*/final_scores_table*.txt`. Full long-format numbers: `summary.csv`.

## Definitions (from `archive/sac_code_drive/scripts/test/prediff_test.py`, `pysteps_test.py`)

- Rain / no-rain threshold: **1 mm/h** (pixel counts as rain if rate >= 1.0), IMERG 0.1 deg grid, 30-min frames, 7 input frames -> 6 forecast frames (+30 ... +180 min).
- POD = H/(H+M), FAR = FA/(H+FA), CSI = H/(H+M+FA), computed per forecast frame of each sequence, then averaged over sequences (mean of per-sequence scores, not pooled counts).
- FSS = 1 - MSE(Pf, Po) / (mean(Pf^2) + mean(Po^2)), Pf/Po = rain fractions in a square moving window of 1, 2, 4, 8 pixels (labelled 11, 22, 44, 89 km using 0.1 deg x 111 km); same threshold. The 11 km value is pixel-scale.
- INDRA-Sat-Diff: one diffusion sample per sequence (no ensemble), back-transformed from log1p scaling (clip 100 mm/h). With KA = knowledge-alignment guidance whose target is 2 x the mean intensity of the input frames; no KA = same weights, guidance off.
- Persistence: last observed frame repeated for all six lead times.
- PySTEPS: STEPS nowcast, Lucas-Kanade motion, **mean of 50 ensemble members**, no velocity perturbation, precip_thr 1 mm/h. Run on the validation folders only; there is no PySTEPS run on the test sets.
- Caveat: the PySTEPS script cuts the file list into fixed 13-frame blocks and uses pysteps' own score functions (undefined scores are NaN and skipped), while the diffusion script scans for contiguous sequences and uses an epsilon (undefined scores become 0, or FSS 1). The two runs therefore have slightly different Persistence values; PySTEPS differences to Persistence below use the Persistence of the PySTEPS run.

## Headline takeaways (numbers computed from the tables; differences are absolute score differences)

- **Validation 2022-2023, full model vs Persistence:** with-KA CSI beats Persistence in 0/12 region x lead-time cases (difference -0.094 to -0.038); FSS (all four scales) beats Persistence in 0/48 cases (-0.124 to -0.035).
- **Validation 2022-2023, why:** with-KA POD is above Persistence in 6/12 cases (-0.027 to +0.043), but its FAR is lower (better) than Persistence in only 0/12 cases (FAR difference +0.091 to +0.144).
- **Validation 2022-2023, effect of KA:** KA raises POD in 12/12 cases (+0.012 to +0.061), lowers FAR in 0/12 cases (FAR change +0.024 to +0.055), and improves CSI in 0/12 cases (-0.014 to -0.001).
- **Validation 2022-2023, full model vs PySTEPS:** with-KA CSI beats PySTEPS in 0/12 cases (-0.091 to -0.069) and FSS in 0/48 cases (-0.114 to -0.029). PySTEPS (50-member ensemble mean) beats its own Persistence on CSI in 11/12 cases (-0.011 to +0.041).
- **Test set, full model vs Persistence:** with-KA CSI beats Persistence in 3/12 region x lead-time cases (difference -0.029 to +0.009); FSS (all four scales) beats Persistence in 8/48 cases (-0.022 to +0.005).
- **Test set, why:** with-KA POD is above Persistence in 10/12 cases (-0.014 to +0.081), but its FAR is lower (better) than Persistence in only 3/12 cases (FAR difference -0.006 to +0.081).
- **Test set, effect of KA:** KA raises POD in 12/12 cases (+0.020 to +0.108), lowers FAR in 0/12 cases (FAR change +0.017 to +0.068), and improves CSI in 9/12 cases (-0.011 to +0.036).
- **Test set:** no PySTEPS run exists for this split, so no optical-flow comparison can be made here.

Reading notes:

- No confidence intervals exist in the source tables; differences of a few thousandths should not be called significant.
- The validation and test sets differ strongly in base scores (test-set Persistence CSI is much higher), so the two splits should not be mixed in one comparison.
- There is no PySTEPS result on the test sets, so the model-vs-PySTEPS statement rests on validation only.
